display.purpose: The h1 only. Archivo at normal width and weight 620, left-aligned at roughly half measure, never centred. Deliberately NOT the outgoing site's condensed 88/800 drawer plate.

label.purpose: Geist Mono. Section numbers, figure numbers, dimensions, table headers, form labels, timestamps, prices, plan tags, captions. Never prose. Captions relax the uppercasing and tracking because a sentence in tracked-out caps is decoded rather than read.

shadows.name: shade-1
shadows.purpose: The only elevation on the navbar, and only once scrolled. Elevation is flat by default on this site.

shadows.name: shade-2
shadows.purpose: The mobile navigation panel, which genuinely floats over content.

shadows.name: shade-3
shadows.purpose: The lead dialog. The one thing on the site that is above the page rather than on it.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Reveals, the FAQ keyframe, the modal.

motion.name: ease-seat
motion.purpose: Parts seating into position: the hero plates and the leader-line draw.

motion.name: t-fast
motion.purpose: Hover and focus, gated behind (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine).

motion.name: t-slow
motion.purpose: Section reveals, staggered 60ms across a section's direct children.

motion.name: hero-assembly
motion.purpose: Runs once on load. The plates seat into their exploded positions; they never collapse into the base plate, because the exploded arrangement is the figure.

motion.name: board-cascade
motion.value: 24ms per cell, left to right, once
motion.purpose: The activity record reads as something that accumulated rather than something drawn all at once.

materials.name: none
materials.value: no gradient, no glow, no noise overlay, no glassmorphism, no coloured shadow, no radius above 4px
materials.purpose: Deliberately empty. The outgoing world shipped two tiled feTurbulence grain layers; this one has no ambient material at all. Everything visible is either type, a drawn line, or a ground.

materials.name: figure line weights
materials.value: 1.25px hairline, 1.75px emphasis, square caps, mitre joins
materials.purpose: One weight family across all six figures and the two icon symbols. Icon strokes are set in 24-unit viewBox space so they RENDER at 1.75px once scaled down — one visual weight, not one numeric one.

materials.name: hatch-45
materials.purpose: Section hatching on cut walls in Figure 2, the drafting convention for a cut surface.

narrative.overview:
The site is set as engineering documentation for a system that has to be inspected.

SafeHaul's whole mechanism is four scattered artifacts — an application, qualification documents, a signature, an employment history — becoming one inspectable assembly. That is literally what an exploded parts diagram depicts, so the site is drawn the way technical documentation is drawn: ruled title blocks, section numbers, callout balloons on leader lines, dimension ticks, figure numbers, sources as a numbered apparatus. The hero is not a screenshot floating over a gradient; it is Figure 1, an exploded assembly whose four plates seat into position on load.

Not a blueprint (no cyanotype, no white-on-blue), not paperwork, not nostalgia. Modern documentation, on paper, in graphite. The register is a working engineering office: even light, no atmosphere, everything legible, nothing dramatised.

Colour is the discipline that holds it together. There is NO BRAND COLOUR. The action is near-black. The only three chromatic values on the site each carry exactly one meaning — draft blue is the drawn line and the link, clear green is verified, attend red is attention — and none of the three is ever used to decorate. That is what keeps the page from reading as the category default it replaced: an indigo-to-violet gradient CTA, pill buttons, coloured card shadows and a bento of equal cards.

Every visual is authored. No photography anywhere, by decision: a stock truck photograph would be the one thing on the page that is not a description of the product.
keyCharacteristics: Paper ground (#F7F7F5), graphite ink, and no brand colour anywhere — the primary action is near-black.
Six authored inline-SVG figures in one line-weight grammar: 1.25px hairlines, 1.75px emphasis, square caps, mitre joins.
Every major section opens with a 2px graphite rule and a ruled title block carrying a mono section number; at 1300px the number hangs outside the measure.
Geist Mono as a genuine second voice for everything a document types or numbers, and never for prose.
Flat by default: three shadow tokens, spent only on the dialog, the mobile panel and the scrolled navbar.
Motion is one grammar — parts seat into position — fired once per section and removed entirely under prefers-reduced-motion.
Colour carries meaning or it does not appear: three chromatic values, one meaning each, never decorative.
rules: THE DRAWN-LINE RULE. Structure is drawn in --graphite and --rule. --draft is a line colour — leaders, balloons, focus rings, inline links. It never fills a region behind text.
THE MEANING RULE. --clear means verified or complete. --attend means attention or required. --draft means the drawn line and the link. No fourth meaning, and none of the three is ever decorative.
THE BLACK-ACTION RULE. The primary action is --graphite. On a graphite ground it inverts to a --paper fill with --graphite text. There is no brand colour on this site.

THE TYPED-THINGS RULE. Geist Mono sets figure numbers, section numbers, dimensions, table headers, timestamps, prices and captions. Never prose. Captions relax the uppercasing and tracking, because a sentence in tracked-out caps is decoded rather than read.
THE ELEVEN-PIXEL FLOOR. No text below 11px anywhere, in CSS or inside a figure. This is what forced the scrolling-figure decision rather than a shrinking one.
THE ILLUSTRATION RULE. Any demonstration data a visitor could mistake for a real driver record is labelled as an illustration.
NO AMBIENT DECORATION. No gradients, no glow, no glassmorphism, no noise overlay, no coloured card shadows, no pills, no radius above 4px, no icon-in-a-circle.
--ink-3 IS THE FLOOR, AND ONLY ON --paper. It measures 4.55:1 there and 4.19:1 on --paper-2. Anything quiet on a recessed ground uses --ink-2 instead.
dos: Mark the column or plan that matters with a drawn 2px graphite rule, never with a colour fill.
Give a wide drawing the sheet and put its caption beside it as a title block; cap the drawing near 1:1 so its lettering matches the page's own mono sizes.
Let a drawing scroll sideways below its natural width, inside a role="region" wrapper with tabindex in the MARKUP and a visible hint — then let JavaScript remove the tab stop where nothing overflows.
Use minmax(0, 1fr) for any grid track a figure can sit in; a bare 1fr never shrinks below min-content and will push the figure off the page.
Stagger a section's direct children from one observer on the section. Never nest data-reveal inside data-reveal.
State a limitation in the copy where one exists. The candour is a brand asset and parts of it are test-enforced.
Keep a double hyphen out of any comment in a standalone .svg — it is XML, and naming a CSS custom property there breaks the whole file silently.
donts: Do not add a brand colour, a gradient, a pill, a coloured shadow, or a radius above 4px.
Do not use --draft as a fill behind text, or any of the three meaning colours decoratively.
Do not photograph anything. Every figure is authored line art.
Do not stretch a figure to the full measure — its labels outgrow every other mono size on the page.
Do not shrink a figure below the eleven-pixel floor to make it fit; scroll it instead.
Do not replace the FAQ's hidden attribute with a grid-template-rows animation. display:none cannot be transitioned and the two cannot coexist.
Do not let the hero plates collapse into the base plate. The exploded arrangement is the figure.
Do not invent a testimonial, customer count, time-saved figure, uptime number, certification, or a popularity claim on a pricing tag. None of them exist.
Do not aria-hide the stacked comparison list. Exactly one of the table and the list is ever in the accessibility tree, and hiding both leaves a phone screen reader with neither.
Do not assume section 6, 16 or 18 has the homepage's markup — the server-rendered blog shares this stylesheet and ships no JavaScript of its own.
